text:
maria-support: Hi team — customer (AcmePayments) reports a sudden spike of 429 responses after they rolled a proxy rule yesterday. They've attached a few x-request-id values. Can we confirm whether this looks like client retry noise hitting our quota windows or a server-side throttling change?

emma: thanks — can you paste one of the failing curl commands they used and one raw response header sample? that helps a lot.

maria-support: here's the example they gave: 
```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-3-small","prompt":"ping","max_tokens":5}'
```
Response headers they copied: 
```
HTTP/2 429
content-type: application/json
x-request-id: rq_9b3a2c4f
x-rate-limit-limit: 120
x-rate-limit-remaining: 0
x-rate-limit-reset: 167
```
(They said sometimes remaining shows 0 then back to >0 within a few seconds)

raj: quick note — the customer sits behind a proxy that does client-side retries on connection errors. If the proxy retries without proper backoff we can see short bursts that exhaust the per-key quota bucket even if sustained QPS is low.

emma: can you ask them to run this one for a few minutes and attach the HAR? it will show retry timing. also ask for the full `-v` curl output so we can see connection resets. example command to capture headers repeatedly: 
```
for i in {1..50}; do curl -s -D - -o /dev/null -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/completions -d '{"model":"redwood-3-small","prompt":"x","max_tokens":1}'; sleep 0.1; done
```

maria-support: pinged customer for HAR and the proxy config. they sent three requestids: rq_9b3a2c4f, rq_9b3a2c5a, rq_9b3a2c77. also said their proxy sometimes replays the request with a new id when it hits a 502 from upstream.

ops-bot: Uploaded debug bundle for token: rb-20260301-1795003302 (contains ingress logs and per-key rate windows).

emma: thanks — I'll pull the ingress timeline. initial thought: quota window is 1 minute, limit is 120 req/min for their plan. If their proxy did ~5 quick retries per user request, a short spike could push remaining to 0 and return 429 until the next reset. Need to confirm inter-arrival times.

raj: also check server-side logs for `retry-after` header behavior — we might be returning `x-rate-limit-reset` but proxy ignoring and replaying. If proxy doesn't honor `Retry-After` it amplifies the issue.

maria-support: customer replied with a small HAR and said the retries happened at t=2026-03-01T15:12:22Z, t+0.3s, t+0.7s for one user flow. attaching minimal excerpt below: 
```
15:12:22.123 -> POST -> rq_9b3a2c4f -> 502
15:12:22.423 -> POST -> rq_9b3a2c5a -> 502
15:12:22.823 -> POST -> rq_9b3a2c77 -> 429
```
They said after that the next successful call was at 15:13:22.

emma: that lines up with a 1-minute reset. action items: 
- maria-support: confirm plan quota (per-key) and share account id.
- raj: check our ingress logs for those request ids and the 502s leading up to them. look for upstream 502s in the same minute.
- ops-bot: include per-key token bucket snapshots from the debug bundle.

raj: I'm seeing the three ids in ingress: two 502 upstreams from node-edge and then a 429 from rate limiter at 15:12:22.8. I've attached the snippet to the debug bundle.

maria-support: customer acknowledges their proxy added an aggressive retry rule and will throttle retries + respect `Retry-After`. they're going to run a soft rollout and recheck.

emma: good. for follow-up, we should suggest these mitigations in the support ticket: 
- implement exponential backoff + jitter on proxy retries
- honor `Retry-After` and `x-rate-limit-reset`
- add client-side rate smoothing if possible

maria-support: ticket updated with suggested mitigations and I'm marking this as "waiting on customer". closing the Slack thread but will reopen if they still see 429s after proxy change. :thumbsup:
